summary: order-service p99 rose from ~150ms to ~5.2s with statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders starting 09:00:42. The fault originates in portfolio-service, not order-service (which was not released). Deployment dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, 08:56) added a realised-P&L query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at with no index; against ~48M rows it forces a Seq Scan, driving the shared ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96% and connections from ~61 to ~190 from the 08:50 bucket. order-service, a co-tenant of ledger-db, then suffered connection-pool saturation (~47) and INSERT timeouts. The DBA autovacuum config change (cfg-2903, 08:00) and storage/IOPS degradation (HIST-110 pattern) are ruled out by timing (50-min gap) and flat disk/replication metrics respectively. Best hypothesis: bad_deployment at portfolio-service. Recommend rolling back dep-5905 or adding an index on trades(account_id, executed_at).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Portfolio-service v4.5.0 unindexed query saturates shared ledger-db, starving order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The dep-5905 release of portfolio-service v4.5.0 added a realised P&L query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at with no supporting index. Against the ~48M-row trades table this forces a sequential scan per request, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96% and connections to ~190. order-service, a co-tenant of the same shared ledger-db, then sees its INSERT INTO orders hit statement timeouts, its connection pool fill (~47 in use) and its p99 rise to ~5.2s.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, new trades query, no migration/index) goes live 08:56
New query does Seq Scan on trades (48.2M rows) -> slow queries jump to ~140/min and CPU to ~96% on ledger-db
ledger-db connections climb to ~190; shared DB resources exhausted
order-service, co-tenant of ledger-db, sees pool saturation (~47) and INSERT INTO orders statement timeouts -> p99 ~5.2s, error rate ~9.4%

assumptions: The 08:50-bucket rise (slow queries, CPU, connections, p99) reflects the 08:56 deploy plus leading edge of the same bucket; the deploy is the trigger, not the autovacuum change.
portfolio-service did not separately have a pre-existing index on (account_id, executed_at) that the plan ignored.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Autovacuum config change cfg-2903 degrades ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The DBA's more-aggressive autovacuum change (scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1) at 08:00 caused vacuum activity that degraded ledger-db, producing the observed CPU/connection saturation and downstream order-service timeouts.
assumptions: Autovacuum, not the new seq-scan query, is the dominant CPU consumer.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Config change at 08:00 precedes the 08:50-08:58 onset by ~50 minutes with no symptom in between (CPU/connections/p99 flat until 08:50). Slow-query log attributes the load to portfolio-service seq scans, not autovacuum, and CPU saturates exactly when those queries start.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db storage/IOPS throttling (infrastructure).
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Cloud volume IOPS throttling on ledger-db (as in HIST-110) degraded query latency and produced downstream timeouts.
assumptions: Burst credits exhausted despite flat disk usage.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: disk_used_pct flat ~71% and replication_lag_ms flat ~40ms throughout; the slow queries are attributable to an unindexed seq scan from portfolio-service, not storage latency.

facts.statement: Only one deployment occurred in the incident window: dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) at 08:56, adding an unindexed trades query; no order-service deployment.
ledger-db slow queries began 08:58:38 with 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) application_name=portfolio-service', from ~1/min to ~140/min.
ledger-db CPU rose ~30% -> ~96% and connections ~61 -> ~190 from the 08:50 bucket onward.
order-service p99 ~150ms -> ~5.2s, error rate ~0.2% -> ~9.4%, db_pool_in_use ~14 -> ~47; 284 INSERT INTO orders statement timeouts from 09:00:42.
ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
Autovacuum config change cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00, ~50 min before onset.
ledger-db disk_used_pct (~71%) and replication_lag_ms (~40ms) stayed flat throughout.

assumptions: The 08:50-bucket aggregates include the leading edge of the same event triggered by the 08:56 deploy; the tight temporal match (deploy 08:56, first slow query 08:58:38, first portfolio warning 08:59:39, first order timeout 09:00:42) supports the deploy as trigger.
No separate portfolio-service deployment or change preceded 08:56 that could produce the same query.
The trades table has no index on (account_id, executed_at) that the planner could have used.

timeline.event: ledger-db slow_queries/CPU/connections and order-service p99 begin rising (08:50 bucket)
dep-5905 portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployed (new unindexed trades query)
First ledger-db slow query: Seq Scan on trades from portfolio-service (8690ms)
First portfolio-service 'holdings P&L query took 7459ms' warning
First order-service statement timeout on INSERT INTO orders

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) or disable the realised-P&L endpoint immediately
recommended_actions.rationale: Removing the unindexed seq-scan workload is the direct trigger; ledger-db CPU and order-service latency should recover within minutes.

recommended_actions.action: Add index on trades(account_id, executed_at) before re-enabling the feature
recommended_actions.rationale: The query filters by account_id + executed_at ordered by executed_at; an index eliminates the 48M-row seq scan.

recommended_actions.action: Add query-plan/index review gate for new queries against large shared tables (trades)
recommended_actions.rationale: Same failure mode as HIST-111; a pre-merge EXPLAIN gate would catch unindexed scans.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and CPU with per-application attribution
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset was detectable at 08:50-08:58; per-app attribution would have named portfolio-service immediately.

recommended_actions.action: Consider isolating heavy analytical/reporting queries away from the shared transactional ledger-db (read replica)
recommended_actions.rationale: Co-tenancy of order-service and portfolio-service on one DB makes any heavy query a cross-service risk.

data_gaps: get_deployments for order-service returned 503 (backend unavailable) after 3 attempts, so order-service-specific deployment history could not be independently confirmed; the all-services deployment query (tc-001) showed no order-service deployment in the window.
No ledger-db error/critical logs were returned (0 matches) — only WARN slow-query lines; absence of ERROR-level DB logs does not prove nothing else occurred.
Exact index definitions on the trades table were not directly inspected; the unindexed-status inference rests on the logged 'Seq Scan on trades' plan.
